title: 3. Bayesian calibrations and reconstructions
text: simulate 50 observations intermediate error scenario. true values alpha = 0.268 beta = 0.0369. start errors model: first table summarizes posterior distribution parameter. second table checks convergence. look max_Rhat 1.01, min_ESS least 100 per chain, divergences. cal.bayesian() gives warning model fails checks. happens, try larger numSavedSteps check data outliers wrong units.
code: set.seed(3) ds <- cal.dataset(error = "S2", nobs = 50) fit <- cal.bayesian(calibrationData = ds, models = "errors") fit #> Bayesian clumped isotope calibration #> Priors: alpha ~ N(0.231, 0.065), beta ~ N(0.039, 0.004) #>  #> BLM1_fit #>         mean     sd   2.5%  97.5% #> alpha 0.2589 0.0214 0.2160 0.2995 #> beta  0.0375 0.0018 0.0341 0.0411 #> sigma 0.0247 0.0028 0.0196 0.0310 #>  #> Convergence #>     model max_Rhat min_ESS divergences #>  BLM1_fit   0.9993    5838           0

code: myPriors <- list(alpha = c(0.25, 0.05), beta = c(0.038, 0.003)) quantile(cal.prior("Informative", n = 10000)$beta, c(0.025, 0.975)) #>       2.5%      97.5%  #> 0.03105497 0.04668649 quantile(cal.prior(myPriors, n = 10000)$beta, c(0.025, 0.975)) #>       2.5%      97.5%  #> 0.03203628 0.04367196 fitWeak <- cal.bayesian(calibrationData = ds, models = "errors", priors = "Weak")  rbind(   Informative = quantile(cal.draws(fit)$beta, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)),   Weak = quantile(cal.draws(fitWeak)$beta, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)) ) #>                   2.5%        50%      97.5% #> Informative 0.03413404 0.03745101 0.04105367 #> Weak        0.03244945 0.03677519 0.04110373

title: 4. Calibrations with a second predictor
text: calibration dataset needs usual columns plus Ion. Ion measured error, also need uncertainty (1 SD). simulate 100 observations Ion raises D47 0.005 per unit. add measurement error Ion SD 0.1.
code: set.seed(3) ds <- cal.dataset(error = "S1", nobs = 100)  trueIon <- rnorm(nrow(ds)) ds$D47 <- ds$D47 + 0.005 * trueIon ds$IonError <- 0.1 ds$Ion <- trueIon + rnorm(nrow(ds), 0, ds$IonError)

title: 4. Calibrations with a second predictor
text: cal.ion.bayesian() accounts errors Temperature, D47, Ion. IonError can single value samples one value per sample. gamma slope Ion. posterior close simulated value 0.005. Ion known without error, leave IonError:
code: fit <- cal.ion.bayesian(calibrationData = ds, IonError = ds$IonError) fit #> Bayesian clumped isotope calibration #> Priors: Flat  #>  #> BLM1_fit #>         mean     sd   2.5%  97.5% #> alpha 0.2725 0.0097 0.2536 0.2910 #> beta  0.0366 0.0008 0.0351 0.0382 #> gamma 0.0051 0.0013 0.0025 0.0075 #> sigma 0.0136 0.0010 0.0118 0.0157 #>  #> Convergence #>     model max_Rhat min_ESS divergences #>  BLM1_fit        1    2348           0 fitKnown <- cal.ion.bayesian(calibrationData = ds) fitKnown #> Bayesian clumped isotope calibration #> Priors: Flat  #>  #> BLM1_fit #>         mean     sd   2.5%  97.5% #> alpha 0.2723 0.0098 0.2533 0.2917 #> beta  0.0367 0.0008 0.0351 0.0382 #> gamma 0.0050 0.0012 0.0026 0.0074 #> sigma 0.0136 0.0010 0.0117 0.0158 #>  #> Convergence #>     model max_Rhat min_ESS divergences #>  BLM1_fit   0.9999    2776           0

title: 4. Calibrations with a second predictor
text: reconstruction dataset needs Ion sample, IonError account uncertainty: useIonError = TRUE, error Ion included reconstructed temperatures: useIonError = FALSE, Ion treated known: rec.bayesian(), error (1 SD) includes uncertainty calibration, scatter around calibration line, error D47.
code: recData <- data.frame(   Sample = paste("Sample", 1:3),   D47 = c(0.6, 0.7, 0.8),   D47error = 0.01,   Ion = c(-1, 0, 1),   IonError = 0.1 ) rec.ion.bayesian(calModel = fit, recData = recData, useIonError = TRUE) #>     Sample D47 D47error  meanTemp    error #> 1 Sample 1 0.6     0.01 59.179098 8.545411 #> 2 Sample 2 0.7     0.01 19.941494 5.798269 #> 3 Sample 3 0.8     0.01 -8.170901 4.334123 rec.ion.bayesian(calModel = fit, recData = recData, useIonError = FALSE) #>     Sample D47 D47error  meanTemp    error #> 1 Sample 1 0.6     0.01 59.160601 8.639737 #> 2 Sample 2 0.7     0.01 19.739268 5.778040 #> 3 Sample 3 0.8     0.01 -8.261234 4.350976

title: 2. Frequentist calibrations and reconstructions
text: simulate 50 observations intermediate error scenario. true values alpha = 0.268 beta = 0.0369. summarize model mean 95% interval slope:
code: set.seed(3) ds <- cal.dataset(error = "S2", nobs = 50)  fits <- list(   OLS = cal.ols(data = ds, replicates = 1000),   WOLS = cal.wols(data = ds, replicates = 1000),   Deming = cal.deming(data = ds, replicates = 1000),   York = cal.york(data = ds, replicates = 1000) ) t(sapply(fits, function(f) {   c(alpha = mean(f$alpha),     beta = mean(f$beta),     beta_lower = quantile(f$beta, 0.025, names = FALSE),     beta_upper = quantile(f$beta, 0.975, names = FALSE)) })) #>            alpha       beta beta_lower beta_upper #> OLS    0.2693856 0.03662650 0.03298794 0.04025965 #> WOLS   0.2642561 0.03705489 0.03369426 0.04073164 #> Deming 0.2612304 0.03731127 0.03346909 0.04101653 #> York   0.2606095 0.03736634 0.03372884 0.04112536

title: 2. Frequentist calibrations and reconstructions
text: cal.ci() takes table alpha beta returns median line 95% interval range temperatures. plot York calibration:
code: ci <- cal.ci(fits$York, from = min(ds$Temperature), to = max(ds$Temperature))[[1]]  plot(D47 ~ Temperature, data = ds, pch = 16, col = "grey50",      xlab = expression(10^6 / T^2 ~ (K)), ylab = expression(Delta[47])) polygon(c(ci$x, rev(ci$x)), c(ci$ci_lower_est, rev(ci$ci_upper_est)),         col = adjustcolor("steelblue", 0.3), border = NA) lines(ci$x, ci$median_est, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
